title: CG 53469 — Quibell 1902 primary excavation context and phallus-sheath correction

primary_source.author: J. E. Quibell
primary_source.title: Note on a Tomb Found at Tell er Roba

established: Before official intervention, local workmen removed more than 350 shabtis and probably other unknown objects.
In the protected burial the shabtis and amulets were above a limestone slab while the gold was on the body below.
The recovered gold formed an integrated funerary body-trapping suite.
Quibell explicitly reports rough gold-foil sheaths covering fingers, toes and phallus.
The Metropolitan Museum independently identifies Cairo CG 53465-53469 as the gold-leaf trappings of the mummy in this Mendes burial.

epistemic_correction.previous_open_question: Could CG 53469 contain ancient organic or paired basal material beneath its gold skin?
epistemic_correction.current_answer: Still open and testable by non-destructive imaging.
epistemic_correction.new_constraint: If organic material survives inside CG 53469, the default interpretation must first be tissue, resin, packing or funerary material associated with the deceased whose body carried the sheath, not a literal Osiris relic.
